world.topic:
Measure check before round N5 of improving the paper-writing worker of rw_313df9cf84a4: the workers of its positions
paper-repo and internal-review-repo. No worker is changed or made in this round, and nothing is released: no
diagnosis, no candidate, no put-back, no approval.

**The one question.** Can the judging that round N5 will use tell apart two workers known to differ? They are **W1**
and **W2**. What each is, and its files, are in a resource given only to the task-setter; no other position is told,
and nothing a position writes says which label is which worker before the label table is published.

## Tasks

- Each task is one paper, written in a world continued from that paper's world at c0, with only the two workers set
  (to W1 or to W2), the continued world's own `delivery.required_paper_files` given again
  (["workspace/submission/manuscript.tex", "workspace/submission/manuscript.pdf"]; the task-setter checks it in
  `config show` of every run world before driving), `"resources": []`, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns
  and 1800 model seconds, worker.image sha256:1c386c95ad418958d152047d267775b0ef0ee7813594751b539bf3bebb1e2abd and
  each paper's environment image as its world records it (paper_45
  sha256:1a1fe2c82ea277a5b0b7fac33ac2001c67dfd15bb1c57ca5dd15cbfa5722d60a, paper_32
  sha256:7ef042b9fda6f1e98bc0a81d64b93edf36d8dbd229b17d5e88116b0a25db882f, paper_17
  sha256:7a8b1bb91072c88ae18adafdead9d2198d53b823dfaf3f54d1e20ac107632b84). Both workers run with the same provider
  and authentication.
- Papers: paper_45 (rw_5c4743418b6b), paper_32 (rw_686e5b0bd6da), paper_17 (rw_e263f2a52297) in the state root
  issue-396-heldout. Do not use paper_29 (rw_313df9cf84a4's own paper).
- **1 run of each worker per paper (6 runs)**, all made in this world and driven at once.
- The task-setter's creation script records every world it makes before driving any. A world it makes that is not
  driven is excluded with its reason. No world is adopted into a slot after the fact.

## A failed run

A run whose world ends without a verified release (`finish` recorded it; `stop --release` or a driver ending
`insufficient-budget` is not a release) is a **failed run**. It is never judged from a draft. It is reported with
its world id, how it ended, its turns and model seconds, and it loses its pair; if both runs of a pair fail, the
pair is a tie.

## What is measured

A **blind paired judgement**, as round N5 makes it:

- For each paper the task-setter makes one pair, the W1 run and the W2 run (3 pairs), and keeps the key. Each pair
  is a judging item: two manuscripts of the same paper under two new labels, in an order the task-setter draws.
- The judge reads both manuscripts in full and the paper's writing material, and says which is the better
  submission of that paper, or that neither is. A decision gives at least two verbatim quotations from each
  manuscript that decide it, each with the material (file and location) that shows the quoted passage is better or
  worse supported, stated or placed. A judgement without them is sent back, not counted.
- **Each pair is judged twice, in opposite orders, under different labels, in different judging turns.** The judge
  does not know which items repeat. A pair is a **win** for a worker only when both readings choose that worker's
  manuscript. Any other outcome is a **tie**. The **disagreement rate** is the share of pairs whose two readings
  differ.

No calibration pair, no verifier, rubric or defect count is asked in this round.

## How the round ends

After every judgement is pushed, the task-setter publishes the label table. The round reports each pair's two
readings and its outcome, the wins, the ties and the disagreement rate, and then stops. No test is applied and
nothing is approved or released; the maintainer reads the result.

## How the judging is made trustworthy

- **Reading.** At most 2 judging items (4 manuscripts) per judging turn. Each manuscript is printed whole before its
  judgement is written, and the judgement is pushed before the next item is opened.
- **Blind.** The judge receives, per label, the manuscript and its paper's writing material only. It holds no world
  resource and reads no run world, verifier output or account of how the workers differ until every judgement is
  pushed; it reads no worker's files. The label table's sha256 is published before the first judgement. The table
  itself is published after the last judgement, and no judgement changes after it.
- **One judge line.** Codex gpt-6.1-sol, effort high, through HuTian's own Codex login, no fallback. A change of
  judge line restarts all judging.

## Positions' work this round asks for

- **judge**: one judging item (one pair) at a time, each manuscript printed whole before its judgement, pushed before
  the next item is opened, at most 2 items per turn. No script writes or keeps a judgement. A judgement says "read in
  full" only when it was.
- **task-setter**: records every world before driving it, adopts none afterwards, and hashes the label table it
  publishes (checks the bytes it hashed are the table it publishes). It gives every continuation the continued
  world's delivery requirement and checks `config show` before driving.
- **coach**: no approval is asked.

## What stays as it is

The target world and its positions; the task settings above; the held-out isolation; W1 and W2 byte for byte (the
sha256 the task-setter records before any run); the release gates of the kernel and of DojoWorld; and every earlier
world, which no position changes.

## Budget

6 runs at 1800 s each (driven at once), 6 pair readings, each about 2 × 180 judge model seconds, and one provider
stall: about 9000 s for this world, of which about 2200 judge model seconds.
